sourceBinding.scope: Private bounded forced-GC batching after all original context/worker/access retirement fences. Default off. All isolates collect together every fourth boundary or at64MiB capped summed heap/external budget. Actual memory pressure honored every boundary.
sourceBinding.advance: At least10% lower complete TodoMVC time at one and four workers in both orders, no more than5% regression in another cell, no isolation/resource failures. Final 2x goal remains separate.
controls: eight fresh contexts with worker/blob/pending-operation retirement
video owner cleanup and moving trusted input across eight contexts
native trace observes both skipped and forced collections
large external allocation triggers heap-budget collection before fourth retirement
complete original application comparisons and cgroup memory

retainedFailures: First public control passed all8 contexts but native startup trace was not published before shutdown. Corrected diagnostic-only controls wait for trace publication; timing runs contain no tracing or added waits.
Initial screenshot decoder command could not import optional Pillow. Existing pinned PNG decoder subsequently verified all16 actual screenshots without rerunning browser work.

decision.action: Reject this batching policy as a broad speed optimization and restore the preceding native sources; retain the negative screen.

limitations: Two applications and two opposite-order blocks, not the final nine-scenario eight-pair confidence gate.
64MiB triggers collection from V8 heap/backing-store observations; it does not bound Blink/native/media/GPU/process memory.
No callback beacon was observed in either finalizer control. The controls test absence of late effects, not proof that a FinalizationRegistry callback executed or drained.
Original request profiling includes waiting/scheduling; context-close duration is not guaranteed removable collection cost.
Cgroup CPU deltas cover fixture startup through fixture shutdown; memory.peak is the charged cgroup maximum observed at owner shutdown. Final resource custody is not admitted.
No public default, release or broader browser/platform admission.
